bull.b: Revenue and profitability have recovered from the 2021–2022 losses, while Q2 revenue reached $1.86B and net income more than doubled year over year. This earnings base across Las Vegas, Macau and Boston supports reinvestment and indicates broad operating momentum over coming quarters.

TTM operating cash flow of about $1.61B and positive free cash flow of about $0.77B provide internal funding for development, dividends and buybacks. Approximately $4.0B of cash and revolver availability further strengthens near-term liquidity and resilience while projects advance.

Macau’s amended land concession authorizes a five-star hotel, theater, event and entertainment center, with completion required within 60 months. This expands non-gaming capacity and deepens Wynn’s position in a core resort market, supporting longer-term diversification beyond casino revenue.

bear.b: Debt of about $12.3B and TTM shareholders’ equity of roughly negative $0.9B leave the group heavily debt-supported. This weak capital structure reduces financial flexibility, raises refinancing sensitivity, and can constrain funding available for resort expansion or shareholder returns if conditions weaken.

Al Marjan’s budget rose about $600M, requiring Wynn’s 40% share to add roughly $240M of equity, with $525M–$650M still expected for the project and related needs. These requirements compete with Macau investment and increase execution and financing pressure through 2027.

TTM net margin is about 6.1%, below the 2023 peak of roughly 11.2%, while management reported Las Vegas and Macau operating expenses up about 6.2% and 9% year over year. Persistent cost inflation can limit operating leverage even as revenue grows.
